title: Swap Two Values
statement:
Swap two values so each variable holds what the other one held. Use a single assignment when your language allows it, and one temporary variable when it does not.

The input is one line with two integers `a` and `b`, each between -1000000 and 1000000, separated by a space. After the swap, print `a` then `b` on one line, separated by a space, so the original `b` comes first. The two numbers can be equal, zero, or negative.

Input:

```text
3 7
```

Expected output:

```text
7 3
```
hints: Some languages let you assign several variables at once, with the values on the right worked out before any of them change.
Without that, keep one value in a temporary variable before you overwrite it.

python.solution:
def swap_values(a: int, b: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    a, b = b, a
    return a, b


a, b = map(int, input().split())
a, b = swap_values(a, b)
print(a, b)
